rules.title: Filing date missing
rules.treatment: Excluded from every duration metric because the clock has no start.
rules.sql: date_of_filing IS NULL

rules.title: Decided case with no recorded outcome
rules.treatment: Kept in duration metrics. Reported as outcome unknown.
rules.sql: decided AND disp_group = 'Missing'

rules.title: First hearing date missing
rules.treatment: Kept. First-hearing date is not used in duration metrics.
rules.sql: date_first_list IS NULL

rules.title: Last hearing date missing
rules.treatment: Kept. Excluded only from the days-since-last-hearing metric.
rules.sql: date_last_list IS NULL

rules.title: Undecided case with no hearing purpose
rules.treatment: Reported in the 'Not a stage / blank' bar of Q1.
rules.sql: NOT decided AND purpose_name IS NULL

rules.title: Judge designation missing
rules.treatment: Kept. Designation is descriptive only in this project.
rules.sql: judge_position IS NULL

rules.title: Petitioner gender not classifiable
rules.treatment: Excluded from the denominator of women's share in Q6, and the excluded share is reported.
rules.sql: coalesce(female_petitioner, -9999) < 0

rules.title: Defendant gender not classifiable
rules.treatment: Excluded from the denominator of women's share in Q6, and the excluded share is reported.
rules.sql: coalesce(female_defendant, -9999) < 0

rules.title: Petitioner advocate gender not classifiable
rules.treatment: Excluded from the denominator of women's share in Q6, and the excluded share is reported.
rules.sql: coalesce(female_adv_pet, -9999) < 0

rules.title: Defendant advocate gender not classifiable
rules.treatment: Excluded from the denominator of women's share in Q6, and the excluded share is reported.
rules.sql: coalesce(female_adv_def, -9999) < 0

rules.title: Decision date before filing date
rules.treatment: Excluded from duration metrics. A negative duration has no meaning.
rules.sql: date_of_decision < date_of_filing

rules.title: Filing date outside the file's year
rules.treatment: Kept in counts by file year. Excluded from durations when the filing date falls outside 2010-2018.
rules.sql: date_part('year', date_of_filing) <> year

rules.title: Decision dated after data collection ended
rules.treatment: Excluded from duration metrics. The date cannot be real, and the true date is unknown.
rules.sql: date_of_decision > collection_end

rules.title: Date earlier than 1950
rules.treatment: The bad date is ignored. Rows with a bad decision date also fail V01.
rules.sql: least(date_of_filing, date_of_decision, date_first_list, date_last_list, date_next_list) < DATE '1950-01-01'

rules.title: Last or first hearing dated after data collection ended
rules.treatment: The hearing date is ignored when computing time since last hearing.
rules.sql: (date_last_list > collection_end AND date_last_list <> DATE '5000-01-01') OR date_first_list > collection_end

rules.title: Next hearing more than five years after data collection ended
rules.treatment: Next-hearing date is not used in any metric.
rules.sql: date_next_list > collection_end_plus_5y

rules.title: Unparseable date string
rules.treatment: The value is stored as NULL at load.
rules.sql: date_parse_failures > 0

rules.title: Gender code outside the documented values
rules.treatment: Treated as not classifiable.
rules.sql:
(female_petitioner NOT IN (-9999, -9998, 0, 1)) OR (female_defendant NOT IN (-9999, -9998, 0, 1))
OR (female_adv_pet NOT IN (-9999, -9998, 0, 1)) OR (female_adv_def NOT IN (-9999, -9998, 0, 1))

rules.title: Last-hearing date is the placeholder 5000-01-01
rules.treatment: Read as missing. It is not used in any duration, and the stale-case check compares earlier dates only.
rules.sql: date_last_list = DATE '5000-01-01'

rules.title: First hearing before filing
rules.treatment: Kept. First-hearing date is not used in duration metrics.
rules.sql: date_first_list < date_of_filing

rules.title: Last hearing before first hearing
rules.treatment: Kept. Time since last hearing uses the last-hearing date alone.
rules.sql: date_last_list < date_first_list

rules.title: Last hearing after the decision
rules.treatment: Kept. Decision date is used as the end of the case.
rules.sql: decided AND date_last_list > date_of_decision AND date_last_list <> DATE '5000-01-01'

rules.title: Undecided case with an outcome recorded
rules.treatment: Kept as open (censored). Counted separately so pendency can be read with and without them.
rules.sql: NOT decided AND disp_group <> 'Missing'

rules.title: Decided case with a later hearing scheduled
rules.treatment: Kept. Next-hearing date is not used in any metric.
rules.sql: decided AND date_next_list > date_of_decision

rules.title: Never-decided case with no hearing in the two years before the cut-off
rules.treatment: Kept as open. Could be real inactivity or an unclosed record, so it is reported as a stale share.
rules.sql: NOT decided AND date_last_list < cutoff_minus_2y

rules.title: Case-ID year differs from the file year
rules.treatment: Kept. Case IDs are used only for joining.
rules.sql: TRY_CAST(right(ddl_case_id, 4) AS INTEGER) <> year

rules.title: Closed with a generic label such as 'disposed'
rules.treatment: Kept in duration metrics. Excluded from any outcome reading.
rules.sql: decided AND disp_group = 'Generic ''disposed'''

rules.title: Closed by transfer or committal rather than a resolution
rules.treatment: Counted as closed in the main curves, to match official disposal counts. Removed in the sensitivity curve.
rules.sql: decided AND disp_group = 'Transferred / committed'

rules.title: Decided after the 2018 cut-off
rules.treatment: Counted as open on the cut-off, because only some courts were collected again after January 2019.
rules.sql: date_of_decision > analysis_cutoff AND date_of_decision <= collection_end

rules.title: Duplicate case ID
rules.treatment: Only the first row per ID would be kept in the analysis table.
rules.sql:
WITH d AS (SELECT ddl_case_id, count(*) AS n, min(state_code) AS state_code, min(year) AS year
           FROM cases GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1)
SELECT state_code, year, sum(n - 1) AS failures FROM d GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Rows identical on every field except the ID
rules.treatment: Kept. Many are genuine batch filings (one complainant, many cases), which rows alone cannot separate from double entry.
rules.sql:
WITH g AS (
    SELECT state_code, year, count(*) AS n
    FROM read_parquet('{cases_year}')
    WHERE date_of_filing IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY state_code, dist_code, court_no, year, judge_position, type_name, purpose_name, disp_name,
             date_of_filing, date_of_decision, date_first_list, date_last_list, date_next_list,
             female_petitioner, female_defendant, female_adv_pet, female_adv_def
    HAVING count(*) > 1
)
SELECT state_code, year, sum(n - 1) AS failures FROM g GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: State code absent from the state key
rules.treatment: The case would stay in national totals and drop out of state views.
rules.sql:
SELECT f.state_code, f.year, count(*) AS failures
FROM fact f ANTI JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT state_code FROM cases_state_key) k USING (state_code)
GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: District code absent from the district key
rules.treatment: The case stays in state totals and drops out of district views.
rules.sql:
SELECT f.state_code, f.year, count(*) AS failures
FROM fact f ANTI JOIN dim_district k USING (state_code, dist_code)
GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Court code absent from the court key
rules.treatment: Kept. Court names are not used in the headline metrics.
rules.sql:
SELECT f.state_code, f.year, count(*) AS failures
FROM fact f ANTI JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT state_code, dist_code, court_no FROM cases_court_key) k
     USING (state_code, dist_code, court_no)
GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Case-type code absent from the type key for that year
rules.treatment: Placed in the 'Other / unmapped' case category.
rules.sql:
SELECT c.state_code, c.year, count(*) AS failures
FROM cases c ANTI JOIN map_type k ON c.type_name = k.type_name AND c.year = k.year
WHERE c.type_name IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Purpose code absent from the purpose key for that year
rules.treatment: Placed in the 'Not a stage / blank' bar of Q1.
rules.sql:
SELECT c.state_code, c.year, count(*) AS failures
FROM cases c ANTI JOIN map_purpose k ON c.purpose_name = k.purpose_name AND c.year = k.year
WHERE c.purpose_name IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Case with no act or section record
rules.treatment: Kept in overall metrics. Shown as 'No act record' in Q3.
rules.sql: SELECT state_code, year, count(*) AS failures FROM fact WHERE NOT has_act_row GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Act record with no matching case
rules.treatment: Ignored, because all analysis starts from the case table.
rules.sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT substr(ddl_case_id, 1, 2) AS state_code, count(*) AS rows_in_acts FROM acts GROUP BY 1),
     m AS (SELECT state_code, count(*) AS matched FROM fact WHERE has_act_row GROUP BY 1)
SELECT a.state_code, NULL::INTEGER AS year, a.rows_in_acts - coalesce(m.matched, 0) AS failures, a.rows_in_acts AS checked
FROM a LEFT JOIN m USING (state_code)

rules.title: Act label blank, not an act name, or implausible
rules.treatment: Shown as its own group in Q3 and never forced into a real act.
rules.sql: SELECT state_code, year, count(*) AS failures FROM fact WHERE has_act_row AND act_family = 'Unknown' GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Act label not mapped to a canonical act
rules.treatment: Shown as 'Other / unmapped' in Q3. The mapping table lists every label for review.
rules.sql: SELECT state_code, year, count(*) AS failures FROM fact WHERE act_canonical = 'Other / unmapped' GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Filed only under a procedural code (CrPC or CPC)
rules.treatment: Kept, but the underlying law cannot be identified, so Q3 reports these separately.
rules.sql: SELECT state_code, year, count(*) AS failures FROM fact WHERE act_family IN ('Criminal procedure', 'Civil procedure') GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Criminal case with no judge link
rules.treatment: Excluded from Q4 only. DDL states that links exist only for criminal cases and match 50-75% of them.
rules.sql:
SELECT state_code, year, count(*) FILTER (NOT has_judge_row) AS failures, count(*) AS checked
FROM fact WHERE criminal = 1 GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Filing judge missing from the judge table
rules.treatment: Excluded from the tenure-based part of Q4.
rules.sql:
SELECT f.state_code, f.year, count(*) FILTER (j.ddl_judge_id IS NULL) AS failures, count(*) AS checked
FROM fact f LEFT JOIN judges j ON f.filing_judge = j.ddl_judge_id
WHERE f.has_judge_row
GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Filing date outside the filing judge's tenure
rules.treatment: Excluded from the tenure-based part of Q4.
rules.sql:
SELECT f.state_code, f.year,
       count(*) FILTER (f.date_of_filing < j.start_date OR f.date_of_filing > j.end_date) AS failures,
       count(*) AS checked
FROM fact f JOIN judges j ON f.filing_judge = j.ddl_judge_id
GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Case in a court with no Census 2011 population link
rules.treatment: The state total keeps the case. District per-lakh figures cannot include it (statewide tribunals).
rules.sql:
SELECT f.state_code, f.year, count(*) AS failures
FROM fact f JOIN dim_district d USING (state_code, dist_code)
WHERE d.population IS NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Judge tenure ends before it starts
rules.treatment: The judge row is excluded from the tenure-based part of Q4.
rules.sql:
SELECT state_code, NULL::INTEGER AS year, count(*) FILTER (end_date < start_date) AS failures, count(*) AS checked
FROM judges GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Case-type label not mapped to a category
rules.treatment: Shown as 'Other / unmapped' in the survival curves.
rules.sql: SELECT state_code, year, count(*) AS failures FROM fact WHERE type_category = 'Other / unmapped' GROUP BY 1, 2

rules.title: Hearing label says nothing about the stage
rules.treatment: Shown as 'Not a stage / blank' in Q1 and never spread across real stages.
rules.sql: SELECT state_code, year, count(*) AS failures FROM fact WHERE stage = '11 Not a stage / blank' GROUP BY 1, 2

issues.issue: Only some courts were collected again after January 2019
issues.evidence: Recorded decisions run at about 10 lakh a month through 2018, fall to about 1 lakh a month by April 2019, and a trickle continues to September 2020. Follow-up therefore differs by court.
issues.treatment: Every case is treated as open on 31 Dec 2018 unless decided by then, so no court gains from later collection. See docs/methods.md.

issues.issue: Early years are under-covered
issues.evidence: Rows per filing year rise 3.2x from 4.28M (2010) to 13.72M (2018). Litigation did not triple, so this reflects the spread of digital records.
issues.treatment: Flow rates use 2016-2018 only. Survival results are also reported by filing year because older cohorts look slower.

issues.issue: Disposals of pre-2010 cases are absent
issues.evidence: The data holds only cases filed from 2010, so disposals of older cases are never counted, which understates disposals in every state.
issues.treatment: Clearance rates and years-to-clear are stated as lower bounds and used for comparison between places, not as forecasts.

issues.issue: Five NJDG states and UTs have no separate DDL rows
issues.evidence: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Andaman and Nicobar have no DDL rows. Puducherry and Lakshadweep appear only as districts under Tamil Nadu and Kerala, so their state rows cannot be compared.
issues.treatment: Listed in the Coverage sheet. Excluded from state rankings where they have no DDL flows.

issues.issue: NJDG '>5 years' column is mislabelled
issues.evidence: In Lok Sabha Q.3371 Annexure II, West Bengal shows more cases over 10 years (8,05,149) than over 5 years (7,19,828), so the column cannot be cumulative.
issues.treatment: Stored as 5-10 years. A unit test checks the assumption and the printed totals.

issues.issue: DDL district crosswalk is incomplete
issues.evidence: 96 of 630 DDL districts have no Census 2011 link and one (Delhi South East) is linked to the wrong district.
issues.treatment: Hand-built crosswalk of 96 rows with a link type for each, plus one correction. Districts carved after 2011 count towards their 2011 parent so per-lakh rates stay honest.

issues.issue: Four 'districts' are statewide tribunals
issues.evidence: Maharashtra's family courts, school tribunals, industrial and labour courts and cooperative appellate court appear as district codes.
issues.treatment: They stay in state totals and are left out of district per-lakh figures.

issues.issue: Metadata does not match the files
issues.evidence: female_petitioner is in the files but not the data dictionary. Gender columns use two formats ('0 male' and bare 0). The judge key is named ddl_filing_judge_id rather than the documented ddl_judge_filing_id.
issues.treatment: Loader parses both gender formats, and docs/data_dictionary.md records the real schema.

issues.issue: Public files contain a linkable case number
issues.evidence: cino (the eCourts case number) is present in the public case files, although the DDL page says identifiers need a separate request.
issues.treatment: Dropped at load and never stored in Parquet, so no output can link back to a named case.

issues.issue: Act key counts look rounded
issues.evidence: act_key lists 'The Indian Penal Code' at exactly 20,900,000, a rounded value from a float column.
issues.treatment: Volumes are recounted from the case rows, and the key's counts are not used.

issues.issue: Some acts look like dropdown defaults
issues.evidence: Acts such as 'Absorbed Areas (Laws) Act' and 'Acquired Territories (Merger) Act' carry tens of thousands of cases each and about 4 lakh together. Their names sit near the top of an alphabetical list and district courts rarely apply them.
issues.treatment: Grouped as 'Implausible act' in Q3 rather than treated as real law. The cause is inferred, not proven.

issues.issue: A loose matching rule misfiled 1.8M cases
issues.evidence: An early act-name pattern ('nact$') also matched every squeezed name ending in '-ion act', which sent Land Acquisition, Dowry Prohibition and similar acts to the NI Act.
issues.treatment: Caught by a unit test before any result was used. Fixed, with regression tests for each affected act.

issues.issue: Project plan citations did not match their source
issues.evidence: The plan cites the eCourts India blog for a 1-2% of GDP cost and 30-40 lakh Section 138 cases. The blog says 0.5-1.5% and 54 lakh+ (a full-text index count), and never mentions 30-40 lakh.
issues.treatment: The brief uses the blog's actual range and tests Section 138 against the Supreme Court's 35.16 lakh figure (31 Dec 2019) as well as the blog's count.

issues.issue: Gender is predicted from names
issues.evidence: DDL infers gender with a neural network on names and reports 97% accuracy on samples. The label is male or female only and many names are unclassifiable.
issues.treatment: Share of women is computed on classified names only and the unclassified share is always shown. It should not be read as a count of individuals.

issues.issue: Some districts appear to have incomplete closure records
issues.evidence: In a small group of districts, led by Bihar, almost no case closes within two years, even bail matters, which normally close within days. That points to unrecorded closures rather than slow courts.
issues.treatment: Flagged with a bail-based check. Flagged districts are left off rankings and shaded as no data on the map, and each affected state's median is also reported without them.

issues.issue: Act records are thin for early years
issues.evidence: Act links cover about half of cases filed 2010-2012 but 94-97% from 2015. Overall 14.8M cases (18%) have no act record. The act table also has about 9M rows for 2019-2020 cases with no matching case file.
issues.treatment: Shown as 'No act record' in Q3 and never redistributed. Section 138 is tested both by act and by case-type label.

issues.issue: Women's shares count cases rather than people
issues.evidence: The same advocate appears on many cases, and the name is often unclassifiable: only 13% of defendants' advocates and 46% of petitioners' advocates have a usable label.
issues.treatment: Reported as a share of classified cases, with the unclassified share shown beside it.

issues.issue: A join shortcut lost about 4M act links
issues.evidence: To speed up the join, an early version narrowed the acts table by the last four digits of the case ID, assuming they were the filing year. They differ from it in 8.5% of cases. A left join keeps its row count, so the row-count check passed.
issues.treatment: Caught when reviewing link rates by year, before any result was used. Joins now use the full ID, and integrity tests check the match rate, not just the row count.

issues.issue: Verdict labels are too uneven to compare states
issues.evidence: Only about 30% of criminal closures record a conviction or acquittal, and the share runs from under 10% in some states to over 60% in others. A state conviction rate built on this would mostly measure labelling.
issues.treatment: Verdicts are reported by case type only and are never ranked by state.

issues.issue: Judge postings may be split by court number
issues.evidence: A posting is one judge in one court position, so moving between court numbers in the same complex counts as a new posting. That can shorten the measured time in a post, and states may record it differently.
issues.treatment: Reported as time in a post rather than time in a court. It is used for scale and not ranked in any finding.

issues.issue: The licence in the download differs from the licence on DDL's website
issues.evidence: The license.txt inside the data archive is the Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0, while DDL's data page states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and asks commercial users to request a separate licence.
issues.treatment: This project follows the stricter terms on DDL's page: attribution, non-commercial, share-alike. The archive's text is kept in docs/ddl_license_in_archive.txt. Ask DDL before any commercial use.

issues.issue: Kerala's 'ST' (summary trial) is mapped to Sessions trial
issues.evidence: 54,785 Kerala filings labelled 'st' are decided within 24 months 77% of the time, against 38% for 'sc' (sessions cases). In Kerala, ST is a summary trial before a magistrate, but pipeline/mappings.py maps the label to Sessions trial. Found while reading the delay-risk model's largest errors.
issues.treatment: Open: fixing the rule would change the published Sessions-trial figures, so it is logged first. The delay-risk model also sees the raw label (case_type_label), which keeps the two apart.

issues.issue: Some courts record no decisions in a year in which they file cases
issues.evidence: 2% of the delay-risk model's 2016 test cases come from courts with no recorded decision in 2015. 33% of those cases were decided within 24 months (about 70% in Chhattisgarh and Gujarat, under 1% in Bihar), so a zero is sometimes real and often a gap in decision records.
issues.treatment: Open: the model reads a zero as real history and predicts 17% for these cases. A next version should treat a court-year with filings but no decisions as missing. See docs/error_analysis.md.
